answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake in escrow and earn trust only through repeated trades with independently established peers. A newcomer’s claims are checked against a mirror of several trust graphs; colluding identities cannot cheaply endorse one another because endorsements inherit the endorser’s slashing risk. A fake swarm must buy and immobilize real capital, absorb losses when caught, and wait through glacier probation before gaining access to a valuable haven.
